chunks: And Sulaymān al-Farrāʾ narrated from Ḥarīz, from Zurārah, who said:
I said to Abī Jaʿfar عليه السلام: A man permits his bondwoman for his brother. He said: “There is no harm in it.”
I said: Then if she comes with a child? So he said: “Let him take his child to himself and return the bondwoman to the man.”
I said to him: He did not permit him in that. He said: “He has indeed permitted him, and he cannot be secure that such a thing would occur.”

key_terms.بِوَلَدٍ: with a child; meaning she gives birth
key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ بِهِ: there is no harm in it; it is legally unobjectionable
key_terms.وَلَدَهُ: his child, attributed to the biological father
key_terms.يُحِلُّ: permits or makes lawful in this context

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a man permits his brother access to his bondwoman and she gives birth?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning a man allowing another to have relations with his bondwoman. It states that if a child results, the child belongs to the man who fathered him, while the bondwoman is returned to her owner. The Imam عليه السلام explains that such permission carries the possibility of this outcome.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.4578 - Sulayman al-Farra' narrated from Hariz, from Zurara, who said:

I asked Abu Jafar Imam Muhammad ibn Ali Al-Baqir (as) about a man who permits his brother to have relations with his bondwoman.
Imam (as) said: "There is no harm in it."

I asked: "What if she gives birth to a child?"
Imam (as) said: "Let him take his child and return the bondwoman to her owner."

I said: "But what if he did not permit him to do that?"
Imam (as) said: "By granting permission, he has implicitly allowed it, and he cannot guarantee that such an outcome would not occur."
